# YuvexPay

> YuvexPay is a Brazilian payment gateway. The public REST API at `https://api.yuvexpay.com/v1/*` lets developers accept payments (PIX, credit and debit cards, boleto), issue refunds, move money out via PIX withdrawals, and manage products, customers, statements and webhooks.

All requests authenticate with a YuvexPay API key sent as a Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer ypk_<env>_<kid>_<secret>`. `<env>` is `test` (sandbox) or `live` (production). The same base URL serves both environments.

Write endpoints (`POST /v1/payments`, `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund`, `POST /v1/withdrawals`, `POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/customers`) require an `X-Idempotency-Key` header.

All amounts are in **BRL** as decimal numbers (e.g. `49.90`), not cents.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/quickstart): Create your first payment with a PIX QR code in under 5 minutes.
- [Authentication](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/authentication): API key format (`ypk_<env>_<kid>_<secret>`), scopes, IP allowlist, rotation, and `GET /v1/auth/self` for self-introspection.
- [Idempotency](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/idempotency): The `X-Idempotency-Key` contract: 24h TTL, 100-char limit, scoped per company and environment, payload-mismatch detection. Only `2xx` responses are stored and replayed, plus a `502 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` on a boleto payment: a same-key retry replays that `502` and never submits a second charge. A same-key retry of an earlier card payment request now returns `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` instead of the stored response (`201` or `502`): recover that payment with `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`, or with a create with the same `externalId`, `mode: "hosted"` and `methods: ["CARD"]`, no `card` object or card fields, and a new key.
- [Errors](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/errors): Standard error envelope and the full code list (auth, validation, idempotency, payment, refund and withdrawal codes). `PROVIDER_REJECTED` (`400`) means the payment was refused, with a generic message that does not say why; `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` (`502` or `503`) means retry later; on a boleto payment a `502` means the outcome is not known yet (see the Payments guide), and on a PIX payment a `502` or `503` means the payment was recorded `CANCELLED`, so retry with a new `externalId`. `CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` (`400`) means the request carried card data or asked for `CARD` in headless mode: cards go through the hosted checkout only. `CARD_HOLDER_INFO_REQUIRED`, `CARD_REMOTE_IP_REQUIRED` and `INSTALLMENTS_NOT_SUPPORTED` can no longer be returned. `PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED` (`403`, `details.method`) means a method in `methods` is not enabled for the account; if card payments are enabled for the account but card acceptance is temporarily unavailable, it is returned only when `CARD` is the only method. Split platform codes: `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (`400`, `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`) means a split to an approved platform is above its fee cap; `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` (`400`, `details.recipientCompanyId`) means the platform's approval was withdrawn; `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID` (`403`, no `details`) means the key in `X-Split-Platform-Key` was refused, one answer for every reason; `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`400`, `details.limit`) means a platform connection would take the seller past its limit of active partners.
- [Rate limiting](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/rate-limiting): Per-company limits, response headers (`X-RateLimit-*`), and exponential backoff guidance.
- [Environments](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/environments): Sandbox vs. production. Same URL, different key prefix.
- [Sandbox testing](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/sandbox): Deterministic recipes. **A sandbox payment is never terminal in the `POST /v1/payments` response — a status check about 5 seconds later writes the outcome.** Payment cents, the same for `PIX`, `CARD` and `BOLETO`: `.01` paid, `.02` stays unpaid forever, `.03` cancelled, `.04` expired, `.05` paid (MED is not reachable from the amount), any other cents paid. The cents are read from the payment `amount` you send, before any fee passed to the payer (`passFeeToPayer`). Nothing is charged: a sandbox card goes through the hosted checkout, which accepts any test card number that passes the Luhn check (for example `4111 1111 1111 1111`), never stores the full card number or the security code, and never asks for a 3D Secure challenge; a card charged in sandbox is always recorded as `credit` in `methodData.cardFundingType`, whatever test card number you use, so `debit` cannot be produced in sandbox; a sandbox boleto carries a valid-format test digitable line and barcode, and `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/boleto` returns a generated test PDF that says it must not be paid. Sandbox refunds work for `PIX`, `CARD` and `BOLETO`: payment cents `.02` make the refund fail with `PSP_REFUND_FAILED`, any other cents succeed, read from the payment amount and not from the refund amount. Withdrawal cents `.01` completed, `.02`/`.03` failed, `.04` stays processing, reached synchronously. `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate` forces a terminal status with no wait: `PAID` (default), `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`, `REFUNDED`, `DISPUTED`; sandbox keys only: a production key gets `403 FORBIDDEN`, and a production payment id gets `404` because a sandbox key cannot see it. Splits in sandbox: the invite, accept and split cycle works without the KYC gate. **The split platform connection does not exist in sandbox: `X-Split-Platform-Key` is ignored with a `ypk_test_` key.** **Sandbox sends no webhooks to a configured endpoint, for any event type — poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and use `/simulate` instead.**
- [Payments guide](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/payments): Headless PIX, headless BOLETO, and the hosted checkout (PIX, CARD, BOLETO). Lifecycle from `NEW` to `PAID`/`REFUNDED`. **Card payments are accepted only through the hosted checkout: `POST /v1/payments` rejects a `card` object, `CARD` in `methods` in headless mode (`mode` omitted or `headless`), and any of `deviceInfo`, `remoteIp`, `holderInfo`, `authorizeOnly`, `creditCard`, `creditCardHolderInfo`, `creditCardToken`, `installmentCount`, `installmentValue`, `totalValue` at the top level of the body, with `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`, even without a valid API key; the card data is not stored or logged. To charge a card, create the payment with `mode: "hosted"` and `CARD` in `methods` (`["CARD"]`, or `["PIX", "CARD"]` to let the payer choose), with an `amount` of at least `R$ 5.00`, and redirect the payer to the returned `checkoutUrl`. The checkout collects the card (credit in a single installment, or debit) and runs 3D Secure itself. The result arrives as `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`, `PAYMENT_PAID` or `PAYMENT_CANCELLED`, or poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`.** A hosted card payment that fails 3D Secure, or is refused after it, ends `CANCELLED` (`PAYMENT_CANCELLED` with `reason: payment_failed`); the payer cannot pick another method for it, so create a new payment. Payment links created in the dashboard use the same hosted checkout. Card payments must be enabled for the account; until they are, a create with `CARD` in `methods` returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`. Card acceptance also requires the account owner's e-mail to be confirmed, and YuvexPay's risk controls can suspend it temporarily; on an account with card payments enabled, while card acceptance is unavailable, other methods keep working, the hosted checkout does not offer `CARD` (payments and payment links created earlier included), a create with `CARD` and other methods succeeds without `CARD`, and a create whose only method is `CARD` returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`. Card payments already created with card data through the API keep working: `GET` returns their masked card `methodData`, and webhooks, refunds and chargebacks are unchanged. On a card payment `methodData.cardFundingType` is `credit`, `debit`, or `null` when the funding type is not known (older payments included); webhook bodies do not carry it. Boleto errors on create: `400 PROVIDER_REJECTED` = refused, generic message, payment recorded `CANCELLED`; `503 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` = charge not created, payment recorded `CANCELLED`, retry later with a new `externalId`; `502 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` = outcome not known yet, the payment stays `PROCESSING` (with `methodData: null`) until resolved (15 minutes or more) and then continues or ends `CANCELLED`. **The `502` is stored for the `X-Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key replays that `502` for 24h and never submits a second charge. Send `externalId` on every boleto payment. To recover after a `502`, repeat the request ONCE with the same `externalId` and a new `X-Idempotency-Key`: it returns the existing payment (its `id`) without a new charge; then poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` until it leaves `PROCESSING`, and create a new payment with a new `externalId` if it ends `CANCELLED`.** Do not poll by repeating the create: a same-key repeat replays the same response for 24h. `methodData` is `null` while a boleto payment is `PROCESSING` after a `502`, and on a payment recorded `CANCELLED` before a charge was created. Without `externalId`, a request with a new key creates a new payment, so the payer can end up with two boletos for the same order. A PIX payment whose create returns `502` or `503` is recorded `CANCELLED`: retry with a new `externalId`. **A payment can be split with other YuvexPay companies through the optional `splits` array on creation: `recipientCompanyId`, `type` (`PERCENTAGE` or `FIXED`) and `value`, set at creation only — there is no endpoint to add, edit or remove a split afterwards.** Shares are computed from `amount` (the gross) and the YuvexPay fee is always the originating company's, never apportioned. `netAmount` stays pre-split: the originator keeps `netAmount` minus the sum of the splits. The sum must be `<= netAmount`, otherwise `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET` and nothing is clamped. **Percentage shares round DOWN to the cent and every remaining cent stays with the originating company.** Splitting is opt-in per company pair, per environment and per direction: **the ORIGINATING company invites the recipient by company ID in its dashboard (Configurações > Parceiros de divisão) and the recipient accepts** (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` until it does, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` once it refuses, and a refused pair needs a new dashboard invitation). States are `PENDING`, `ACCEPTED` (the active state), `DECLINED`, `REVOKED` and `CANCELLED` (invite withdrawn by the originator). Either side can revoke an active pair (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`), and **revocation is forward-only, so payments already created still settle, refund and freeze normally.** Re-inviting after `DECLINED`/`REVOKED`/`CANCELLED` creates a NEW relationship and keeps the old one as history. Invite/accept/decline/revoke are dashboard-only — there is no API for them — but `GET /v1/splits/partners` lists the pairs so an integration can discover usable IDs. **The one exception is a split platform approved by YuvexPay: it connects a seller on the seller's first payment, with no invitation, by sending its own API key in `X-Split-Platform-Key` on `POST /v1/payments`, in production only, and every split to it is limited by a fee cap (`SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED`); see the Split platforms guide.** Active partners are capped per company (three by default); that ceiling is enforced in the dashboard at invite/accept time, and the public API returns it only when a platform connection would exceed it (`SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `details.limit`). Both companies must be approved (KYC, plus KYB for a business) at invite time and again when the payment is created; **in sandbox the KYC gate does not apply, so the whole cycle is testable; the platform connection is the exception and does not exist in sandbox.** **Recipients get no webhook and no receipt**: the payment is not theirs, `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` returns `404` for them, and they see the money only in `GET /v1/balance`, in `GET /v1/documents/statements` and in their dashboard. A split credit follows the **recipient's own** rolling reserve policy, not the originator's. Splits are environment-locked (`SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH`).
- [Split platforms](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/split-platforms): For marketplaces and checkouts that create payments with the seller's API key and take a share through `splits`. Approval is granted by YuvexPay, company by company, with a fee cap agreed at approval (contact support). **An approved platform connects a seller on the first payment: `POST /v1/payments` with the seller's key in `Authorization`, the platform's company in `splits[]` and the platform's own key, without `Bearer`, in `X-Split-Platform-Key`. The relationship is recorded as `ACCEPTED` with the cap, the seller is notified, and the payment is created on the same call.** A connection opens no split request and does not count toward the seller's limit of pending requests. A request from the seller that is already pending, a dashboard invitation or one that an earlier payment opened without the header, is accepted by that call. The header is read only on a production request in which exactly one recipient in `splits[]` has no accepted relationship with the seller; otherwise it is ignored, so a connected seller never depends on the platform key. The platform key must be an active production key with `payments:write`, used from inside its IP allowlist, from a company other than the seller's: otherwise `403 SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID`, one answer for every reason. **A call that does not connect follows the regular flow, in production and in sandbox: it returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` and opens a pending request to each recipient that has no relationship with the seller yet and can receive splits in that environment (an active company, in the same environment as the request and, in production, with verification approved); for any other company ID the answer is the same and no request is opened. The platform accepts the request in its dashboard, or a later call with the header accepts it. That is the case without the header, with a valid key whose company is not the recipient or is not an approved platform, and with two or more recipients that have no accepted relationship; past the seller's limit of pending requests the call returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`.** `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID`, `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` and `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` open no request. Send the header from a server only; it is not allowed on cross-origin browser requests. **Fee cap: a percentage of `amount` (the gross). The cap applied is the lowest of the cap recorded on the relationship, the platform's current cap and the maximum YuvexPay allows; a lowered cap applies at once, a raised one does not reach sellers already connected. `PERCENTAGE` must be at most the cap; `FIXED` must be at most `amount × cap / 100`, not rounded up. Above it: `400 SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` with `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`, checked before anything is recorded, so a first payment above the cap connects nobody.** A request the platform accepts by hand in its dashboard is capped too: the relationship records the platform's cap at the time it accepts, returned as `feeCap`, and each split is limited by the same three values. `GET /v1/splits/partners?direction=INCOMING&status=ACCEPTED` lists the sellers connected to the platform; without `status` the list also carries pending, declined, revoked and cancelled pairs. A seller with no active partner slot left gets `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The seller gets a dashboard notification and an e-mail naming the platform and the cap, and can revoke under Configurações > Parceiros de divisão; either side can revoke. A request the platform accepts by hand sends the seller the notice of any accepted invitation, which does not name the cap. **A pair that was revoked, or that the platform once declined, is never reconnected by the header (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED`), even after a later invitation was cancelled: the seller sends a new dashboard invitation and the platform accepts it in its dashboard.** While that invitation is pending, payments return `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`; if the seller cancels it, a payment with the header returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED` or `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` again, and one without the header opens a new pending request and returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`. If YuvexPay withdraws the approval, every new payment with a split to the platform fails with `400 SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` for sellers connected with a fee cap, the header connects no new seller (the call follows the regular flow), and payments already created are not changed. If the approval is given back, connected sellers work again under the same lowest-of-three cap rule, with the platform's new cap. A payment link does not connect a platform: it is refused with `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` and follows the regular flow; once the seller is connected, links follow the same cap. The connection does not exist in sandbox: the approved company is a production company and a sandbox payment can only split to a company in sandbox mode, so a `ypk_test_` payment that names the approved company returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`, opens no request and leaves nothing to accept. To test the split, use a separate company in sandbox mode as the recipient with the sandbox invite flow; no company in sandbox mode is an approved platform, so no fee cap applies there. The seller should give the platform a key limited to the payments scopes with an IP allowlist, never a `*` key.
- [Refunds](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/refunds): Eligibility rules, lifecycle, and error codes (`REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`, `REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `REFUND_REQUIRES_MANUAL_REVIEW`, etc.). Eligibility is enforced by `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund` itself; the payment detail response carries no eligibility field. **A payment can be refunded once, fully or partially: a `PARTIAL_REFUND` payment is not refundable again (`400 REFUND_ALREADY_PERFORMED`), a `REFUNDED` one returns `400 ALREADY_REFUNDED`, and a refund requested while another is being processed returns `400 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`.** **Partial refunds are conditional, not unsupported: they require a payment that has already settled and a processing route that supports them, otherwise `PARTIAL_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED`. A full refund is always available on a refundable payment.** On a payment with splits the refund is proportional: every party is debited in proportion to what it received, the originating company included, and partial refunds use the same proportions. A recipient that already withdrew its share goes negative and the shortfall is never moved onto the originating company, so `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE_FOR_REFUND` is measured against the originating company's share only. A PIX MED freezes each party's proportional share the same way.
- [Withdrawals](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/withdrawals): PIX-only, BRL-only, daily/nightly limits, masked `pixKey`, and the never-retry rule on ambiguous `PROCESSING` (whose horizon is hours, not minutes). **`amount` is the NET the recipient receives; the flat fee is added on top, so the balance is debited `grossAmount = amount + feeAmount`.** Gross is what `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, the daily/nightly `used` counter and the per-transaction cap are measured against; the minimum is measured against the net and is `R$ 10.00` unless raised for the account — read `minAmount` from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`. The creditor document sent to the network resolves in three steps: `destination.recipientDocument` when sent, else the PIX key itself when it is a CPF or CNPJ key, else your own tax id. `creditorDocumentSource` is dashboard-only and returns `400 CREDITOR_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_NOT_SUPPORTED` on the public API. Per-transaction caps are account-dependent and come from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`, not a fixed platform maximum. `errorMessage` is returned by `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` only, never by the list. `providerErrorCode` is on both and carries only a rejection code reported by the receiving institution (`AC03`, `AC06`, `AC07`, `AG03`, `AM18`, `RR04`, `SL02`, `BE01`, `CH11`, `PIX_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, `PIX_KEY_OWNER_MISMATCH`, `ACCOUNT_CLOSED`, `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`), otherwise `null`.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/webhooks): `v1` HMAC-SHA256 signature with timestamp anti-replay (`X-Webhook-Signature`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`), at-least-once delivery, no order guarantees, retries. **The HTTP body is the bare event object — there is no `{ id, type, data }` envelope and the event name is carried only in the `X-Webhook-Event` header.** Twelve subscribable event types. `PAYMENT_PAID` carries a `payer` block (name, CPF/CNPJ, institution name + ISPB) plus the network `endToEndId`; `payer.document` carries a masked string (for example `***405566**`) when no full document is on file, and is `null` only when neither was captured. `WITHDRAWAL_SENT` carries a `recipient` block, populated when the withdrawal had a recipient document. Both blocks are `null` when every field would be null. **Webhooks are delivered for production activity only: sandbox payments and withdrawals send no webhooks to a configured endpoint, for any event type, because an endpoint belongs to the account and not to an environment.** A sandbox integration polls `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and forces terminal outcomes with `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate`; the dashboard **Send test** button delivers a signed `TEST` event to exercise a verifier. `MED_RECEIVED.providerMedId` is always `null` when present, `source` on `PAYMENT_REFUNDED` and `MED_RESOLVED` is `merchant_refund` or `null`, and `PAYMENT_REFUND_FAILED.reason` is always `Reembolso não processado. O valor foi devolvido ao saldo.` `PAYMENT_CANCELLED.reason`, when present, is `payment_failed` (payment refused or not completed, such as a card refused or failing 3D Secure) or `payment_cancelled` (charge cancelled before payment). **When a card chargeback dispute is won, the chargeback debit is credited back (the processing fee stays with YuvexPay), the payment leaves `CHARGEBACK` for the status it had before (`PAID`, `CONFIRMED`, `REFUNDED` or `PARTIAL_REFUND`), and `PAYMENT_PAID` or `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED` is sent again for that status; a payment restored to `REFUNDED` or `PARTIAL_REFUND` sends no webhook.**
- [Changelog](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/changelog): API changes, written in Portuguese. 2026-10-04, breaking: card payments are no longer accepted by `POST /v1/payments` (`400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`), use the hosted checkout; sandbox `CARD` and `BOLETO` follow the payment cents table and sandbox refunds work for every method. 2026-10-04, debit cards: the hosted checkout also accepts debit cards, and card payments returned by `GET /v1/payments`, `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`, `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`, `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate` and a create repeated with the same `externalId` carry the read-only `methodData.cardFundingType` (`credit`, `debit` or `null`); webhooks are unchanged. 2026-10-07, card availability: card acceptance requires the account owner's e-mail to be confirmed and can be suspended temporarily by risk controls; on an account with card payments enabled, while it is unavailable, the hosted checkout does not offer `CARD`, a create with other methods drops `CARD`, and a create with `CARD` as the only method returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`.

## API reference

- [API overview](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/introduction)
- [Inspect API key](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/auth/self): `GET /v1/auth/self`
- [Create payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/create): `POST /v1/payments` — PIX supports `enforcePayerDocument` (best-effort same-document opt-in). `CARD` is hosted only: a `card` object, `CARD` in headless mode, or a card field at the top level of the body returns `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` with the message `Pagamentos com cartão não são aceitos pela API. Use o checkout hospedado: crie o pagamento com mode "hosted" e envie o pagador para o checkoutUrl.`, even without a valid API key. The `card` object and `methodData.challengeUrl` were removed, and `CARD_HOLDER_INFO_REQUIRED`, `CARD_REMOTE_IP_REQUIRED` and `INSTALLMENTS_NOT_SUPPORTED` can no longer be returned. A refused payment returns `400 PROVIDER_REJECTED`; `502` and `503` return `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`. A boleto `502` (outcome not known yet) is stored and replayed for the same `X-Idempotency-Key`: recover the payment by repeating the request once with the same `externalId` and a new key, then poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`. A PIX `502` or `503` is recorded `CANCELLED`. Optional `splits[]` (`recipientCompanyId`, `type`, `value`) shares the payment with other YuvexPay companies; the maximum number of entries is the recipient limit configured for the account, three by default. Split failures arrive as a top-level `error.code`, not inside `VALIDATION_ERROR.details`: `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SPLIT_SELF_RECIPIENT`, `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` (with `details.recipients`, the company IDs that declined), `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED`, `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH`, `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (with `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`), `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` and `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (platform connection only, with `details.limit`) are `400`; `SPLIT_ORIGINATOR_NOT_APPROVED` and `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID` are `403`. Optional header `X-Split-Platform-Key`: the API key of an approved split platform, sent without `Bearer`, which connects the seller to the platform named in `splits[]` on this call; it is read only on a production request in which exactly one recipient has no accepted relationship, and ignored otherwise, sandbox included. **`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` is the single answer for every recipient that cannot receive a split yet except a pair that declined an invitation from your company or was revoked — both need an invitation your company already sent, so a company ID you never invited reads the same whether or not it exists and the error cannot be used to enumerate company IDs.** `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED` and `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH` are only returned for a recipient that had already accepted the relationship. There is no `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`. Outstanding consent requests are capped per company and environment (20 by default): beyond that, naming a new recipient returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`. The response echoes `splits` back with an `id` per entry, `[]` when there are none.
- [List payments](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/list): `GET /v1/payments`
- [Get payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` — paid PIX payments include a nullable `payer` block (name, document, institution name + ISPB) and `paidAt`. CARD payments carry masked card data in `methodData`, without `challengeUrl`, and `methodData.cardFundingType`: `credit`, `debit`, or `null` when the funding type is not known (older payments included). `methodData` is `null` while a boleto payment is `PROCESSING` after a `502`.
- [Get payment by txId](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get-by-txid): `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`
- [Download boleto PDF](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get-boleto): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/boleto`
- [Refund payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/refund): `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund` — a payment can be refunded once; a second refund returns `400 REFUND_ALREADY_PERFORMED` (after a partial refund) or `400 ALREADY_REFUNDED` (after a full one).
- [List refunds](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/list-refunds): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refunds` — `reason` is the one sent with the refund request, or `null` for refunds YuvexPay executed on its own, such as the return of a PIX MED.
- [List split partners](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/splits/partners): `GET /v1/splits/partners` — the companies this account may split with, in both directions, for the environment of the API key. Fields: `id` (the relationship, not the company), `companyId` (send this as `recipientCompanyId`), `tradeName`, `direction` (`OUTGOING`/`INCOMING`), `status`, `feeCap` (the fee cap recorded on a relationship with an approved split platform, in percent of `amount`, as a string with two decimal places, or `null` for an ordinary partner), `requestedAt`, `acceptedAt`. Optional `status` and `direction` filters. Every partner is returned in one response, newest first, unless `limit` (1 to 100) is sent: then at most `limit` relationships are read per call, the response carries `nextCursor`, to send back as `cursor` until it is `null`, and a page can carry fewer partners than `limit`. `nextCursor` is `null` when the whole list was returned. **Only `ACCEPTED` is usable in `splits[]`.** Requires the `payments:read` scope. There is no API to invite, accept, decline or revoke — that is dashboard-only; the one exception is an approved split platform connecting a seller through `X-Split-Platform-Key` on `POST /v1/payments`.
- [Balance](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/balance/get): `GET /v1/balance` — a split credit received from another YuvexPay company follows **your own** rolling reserve policy, not the originating company's. Together with `GET /v1/documents/statements` this is the only public record a split recipient has of the money — the payment itself belongs to the originating company.
- [Create withdrawal](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/create): `POST /v1/withdrawals` — optional `destination.recipientDocument` (CPF/CNPJ of the PIX key holder); send it for any third-party payout.
- [List withdrawals](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/list): `GET /v1/withdrawals` — no `errorMessage` and no `isSandbox`; `providerErrorCode` is present.
- [Get withdrawal](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/get): `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` — carries `errorMessage` and `providerErrorCode`.
- [Withdrawal limits](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/limits): `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits` — daily/nightly window, `minAmount` and `perTransactionLimit`.
- [Create product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/create): `POST /v1/products`
- [List products](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/list): `GET /v1/products`
- [Get product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/get): `GET /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Get product by external id](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/get-by-external-id): `GET /v1/products/external/{externalId}`
- [Update product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/update): `PATCH /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Delete product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/delete): `DELETE /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Upload product image](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/upload-image): `POST /v1/products/{productId}/image`
- [Delete product image](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/delete-image): `DELETE /v1/products/{productId}/image`
- [Create customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/create): `POST /v1/customers`
- [List customers](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/list): `GET /v1/customers`
- [Get customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/get): `GET /v1/customers/{customerId}` — `customerId` is a `cus_*` slug, not a UUID.
- [Update customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/update): `PATCH /v1/customers/{customerId}`
- [Delete customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/delete): `DELETE /v1/customers/{customerId}`
- [Payment receipt](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/payment-receipt): `GET /v1/documents/payments/{paymentId}/receipt` — scoped to the key's environment; an id from the other environment returns `404`.
- [Withdrawal receipt](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/withdrawal-receipt): `GET /v1/documents/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}/receipt` — same environment scoping.
- [Account statement](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/statement): `GET /v1/documents/statements` — built from the real-money ledger, so a sandbox key always gets an empty statement.
